conviction_note: The quarter is largely knowable from the company's own Oct 6 volume/RPC report: options RPC reset to $0.098 (below the ~$0.103-0.11 the CFO framed for H2), a bottom-up net revenue of ~$126-127M against a disputed $129.7M/$135.4M bar and EPS near the $0.37 consensus. The fundamental read is a slight miss. But the stock is -33% since the last print, -45% from its high, -9.9% in five sessions, with upside-paid skew (-4.25) and 3 of 4 prior prints up. So p_up sits barely above 50, and the swing is the Q4 commentary on market share against two new exchanges. The findings sum to -0.2 and the scaled number is +0.28: both are effectively zero, and the small sign gap is the positioning lean against a slightly soft quarter.
bar: Net revenue (revenues less cost of revenues) and adjusted EPS. Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-21 gives consensus adj EPS $0.37 on ~$129.7M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/MIAX/21218). A search-snippet summary of Benzinga's forecast table gives $0.40 on $135.4M (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/MIAX/earnings-forecasts; the page itself returned 403, so this is snippet-only and possibly stale). The two sources disagree, so the bar is disputed and every reported-quarter finding is capped small. There is no company revenue/EPS guide; the only company guide is FY26 adjusted opex $260-270M, SBC $29-32M, D&A $35-39M, capex $40-45M, tax 27-29% (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news/miami-international-holdings-reports-second-quarter-2026-results), plus the CFO's H2 RPC framing of 'closer to the previous few quarters', ~$0.103-0.11 (Q2 call, 2026-08-05, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/).
positioning_check: Short interest: 7.6M shares, 4.46 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (aggregator curvedtrading.com via search snippet; the page itself 403'd). That is about 7.7% of the ~99.2M shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 2026-07-31). It is moderate, not crowded, and three months stale; Sep/Oct settlements were not found. Borrow fee 0.4% (same aggregator, older). Options in the baseline: 25d skew -4.25 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.12, event-implied move 7.72% against a 2.35% median of 4 prior reactions (3 of 4 up), ATM spread 30% of mid (thin chain). Tape: spot $31.54, -9.86% over 5 days, -6.55% over 20 days, -44.5% from the 52w high, +6.7% off the 52w low. Earnings Whispers (2026-10-21) puts the post-Q2 slide near 30% and says sentiment moved from 'decidedly bearish' before Q2 to 'modestly bullish'. AAII (2026-10-29) says -28.8% YTD, with 1 analyst upgrade and 1 downgrade in the past month.

findings.finding: The company's own Volume & RPC report (updated 2026-10-06) prints preliminary Q3'26 options RPC of $0.098 against $0.124 in Q2'26 and $0.110 in Q1'26, on ADV of 11,088k over 64 days. That puts Q3 options net transaction fees at about $69.5M against about $84.5M in Q2 (-18%). A bottom-up Q3 net revenue built on Q2's $141.1M segment split comes to about $126-127M, against consensus of $129.7M (EW) or $135.4M (Benzinga snippet). $0.098 is below the ~$0.103-0.11 the CFO told analysts to expect for H2 on the Aug 5 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 (2026-08-05): RPC 12.4c, net revenue +35%, adj EPS $0.48 vs $0.41 consensus; the next session was -1.09% and the stock then slid ~30% into October. Prior prints were +4.36%, +2.1% and +2.6%. The name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it is priced. The RPC number has been public for 3 weeks, the stock made its post-earnings low ($29.06 per EW) after it, and the EW consensus ($0.37/$129.7M on 2026-10-21) roughly embeds it. What may not be priced is the residual gap between a mechanical ~$126.5M and a $129.7M-$135.4M bar, if some estimates are stale. If it were fully priced, the aggregators would carry one agreeing consensus near $126-127M; they do not.
findings.independence: Q2 segment split and opex guide from the Q2 release (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news/miami-international-holdings-reports-second-quarter-2026-results); CFO H2 RPC framing from the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/). These are separate documents, but all are company-sourced. The offset is that non-transaction fees (access fees rose to $30.8M in Q2 from $22.2M, helped by Sapphire waiver expiry) could keep growing and close the gap.

findings.finding: The RPC reset is industry-wide, not MIAX-specific. Cboe's September 2026 volume report gives multi-listed options RPC of $0.052 projected for Q3'26 against $0.064 for Q2'26 (-19%), in line with MIAX's -21% ($0.124 to $0.098), consistent with the July 1 options regulatory fee (ORF) methodology change the MIAX CFO cited. Cboe reports Q3 before the open on 2026-10-30, inside the window, so the read-through will be explicit on day one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. The 30% slide after Q2 suggests the market has treated the RPC fall partly as MIAX-specific pricing weakness.
findings.why_not_priced: The Cboe RPC line sits in a peer's volume release that MIAX holders may not read side by side. If the market had read MIAX's RPC drop as industry-wide, MIAX would not have underperformed by ~30% since August while Cboe/Nasdaq did not (Nasdaq Market Services net revenue was +2% YoY in Q3). Cboe's Oct 30 print may reinforce this, or may show Cboe defending capture better.
findings.independence: MIAX CFO attributing the RPC change to ORF reform on the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/). Separate company, separate document.

findings.finding: Q3 options volume and share were strong in the reported quarter: MIAX ADV 11,088k (Q2 10,989k), market share 17.4% against 16.5% in Q2. The industry ADV figure in the same report (63.8M) matches Nasdaq's Q3 release; Nasdaq's own matched share slipped to 28.1% from 28.5% YoY. So volume is up quarter on quarter even though RPC fell.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Share and ADV are published monthly; the Q2 share dip to 16.5% was flagged on the Q2 call and the stock fell after it. No print has turned on share alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: monthly releases have been public since early October. Included because the quarterly share number (17.4%) is better than the September exit rate that dominates the narrative.
findings.independence: Nasdaq Q3 release, industry ADV 63.8M and Nasdaq share 28.1% vs 28.5% (https://mondovisione.com/news/nasdaq-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-strong-execution-drives-12-billion-20261022/). Shares a document with finding 1 (same RPC report).

findings.finding: Exit-rate share fell sharply: September options share was 16.7% against 18.4% in August and 17.6% in September 2025. Two new options exchanges launched near quarter-end (Cboe: 20 exchanges, six operators). MEMX's MX2, a customer-priority pro-rata venue (the model MIAX Options runs), launched 2026-09-14 and reached 0.43% total share by Sep 30. That makes the Q4/October share commentary on the call the main forward risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 call management said share had 'rebounded about 17.1% in July' and August looked 'even better' (18.4% realised); the stock still fell ~30% afterwards. Share commentary has not lifted the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The September number is public. What is not public is October-to-date share with MX2 fully rolled out (all symbols from Sep 30) and IEX Options live. MIAX's October volume release (~early November) falls outside the window, so the call is the first look. A priced risk would show as put skew; instead calls are bid (skew -4.25).
findings.independence: MX2 launch and share (https://www.marketsmedia.com/memx-group-completes-rollout-of-mx2-options/, snippet via search). Cboe industry note on two new exchanges (https://www.cboe.com/insights/posts/state-of-the-options-industry-q-3-2026-volume-growth-concentrated-in-index-and-etf-options, 2026-10-19). Short interest is moderate (4.46 days, July), so this negative is not shrunk for a crowded short, but it is shrunk for the upside skew.

findings.finding: MIAX Futures' financial (Bloomberg index) products are not gaining traction: financial futures ADV fell from 5,897 in May (launch) to 1,557 in August and 2,226 in September, at a negative rolling RPC of -$1.43 (incentives exceed fees). Management guided higher marketing spend for these products in H2, and the segment lost $12.7M in operating income in Q2. Retail access (NinjaTrader, announced 2026-10-15) came only in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Futures were flat at $5M net revenue in Q2 and did not visibly move the Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a small segment (~4% of net revenue), so it is mostly ignored. Its relevance is the opex/marketing guide; net of the options business it is a small item.
findings.independence: Q2 call on marketing spend and retail onboarding (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/); NinjaTrader availability (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news?page=0, 2026-10-15). Shares the RPC report with findings 1 and 3.

findings.finding: Pearl equities capture turned positive: rolling capture was $0.010 per 100 shares in Q3 against -$0.001 in Q2, even as share fell to 0.7% from 0.9%. That implies about +$0.7M of equities net transaction fees against roughly zero, so the segment loss ($2.3M operating loss in Q2) likely narrows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Equities is ~4% of net revenue and has never been cited as a driver of a reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small to matter for most models. Filed for completeness and sized net of the options business.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1, 3 and 5. The Q2 call notes August Pearl pricing changes were reverted for not having the expected impact (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out: -33% since the last report, -44.5% from the 52-week high, -9.86% over 5 sessions, 6.7% above the 52-week low. The options market pays for upside (25d skew -4.25, put/call OI 0.12), short interest is moderate (7.6M, 4.46 days at 2026-07-15), and EW reports sentiment moved to 'modestly bullish'. A print roughly at the $0.37 bar against these expectations has room to relieve.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 3 of the last 4 reactions were positive (+4.36, +2.1, +2.6, -1.09); median |move| 2.35%. The option market now implies 7.72%, roughly 3x that history.
findings.why_not_priced: This agrees with the skew, so it is largely priced. Calls are already bid. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: AAII 2026-10-29 (-28.8% YTD, weak momentum; https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/549834-why-miami-international-holdings-inc8217s-miax-stock-is-down-589). The sealed baseline skew and tape are a separate source.

findings.finding: The balance sheet gives room for a capital-return or reinvestment announcement: $660.5M cash and $1.5M debt at 2026-06-30, against a market cap of about $3.1B (99.2M shares at $31.54), so cash is about 21% of market cap. The 10-Q shows only employee-plan share withholding ($17.0M in H1) and no disclosed open-market buyback program.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback has ever been announced at a print, so there is no history.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference: no source says a program is coming. The cash is public. A buyback would be visible as a jump if announced; it is sized near zero because nothing indicates one.
findings.independence: Q2 release cash and debt figures (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news/miami-international-holdings-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). Shares the company's own filings.

outside_window.finding: October 2026 trading results (options share with MX2 and IEX Options fully live, October RPC) arrive in MIAX's monthly release, usually in the first week of November, after the exit window unless management pre-discloses on the call.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The soft reported quarter (RPC below the CFO's H2 framing) and the September share drop cut against the upside-paid skew. The washed-out run-up (-33% since the last print, -9.9% in 5 days) agrees with the skew's call for a relief move. Net is a near-zero sum with p_up barely above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed: EW $129.7M vs Benzinga $135.4M): reported-quarter RPC finding capped smaller, -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 7 (sign against strong upside skew; short interest checked, moderate): September-share/new-exchange negative shrunk, -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 7 / core table (lean agrees with skew, so partly priced): positioning finding shrunk, +1.0 to +0.6; p_up moved 53 to 52.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): futures finding -0.5 to -0.3, equities finding +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 5 (documents beat inference): capital-return inference +0.3 to +0.2; Cboe peer RPC kept as a document-backed finding but trimmed +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company already published monthly): reported ADV/share finding +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold a Q2 beat): kept the reported-quarter findings small; print_vs_bar -1.5 left unchanged.
